Article Title: Narendra Modi becomes second PM to deliver 13th consecutive Independence Day speech
Article Text:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi addresses the nation during the 8oth Independence Day celebrations, at Red Fort in New Delhi. (PTI image)

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday delivered his 13th consecutive Independence Day speech from the ramparts of the Red Fort, becoming the second prime minister after Jawaharlal Nehru to achieve the milestone.PM Modi has addressed the nation from the Red Fort every Independence Day since taking office in 2014. His latest address came on India's 80th Independence Day.Also read: 80th Independence Day - A throwback at PM Modi's signature Red Fort turbans Nehru, India's first prime minister, holds the record for the longest uninterrupted run of Independence Day addresses, having delivered 17 consecutive speeches from 1947 to 1963.PM Modi surpassed former prime minister Indira Gandhi, who delivered 11 consecutive Independence Day speeches between 1966 and 1976.PM Modi hoisted the National Flag at the Red Fort before beginning his address, with the ceremony synchronised with a 21-gun salute by the ceremonial battery.
Article Summary: Pm modi has addressed the nation from the red fort every independence day since taking office in 2014. His latest address came on india's 80th independence day. Pm modi surpassed former prime minister indira gandhi, who delivered 11 consecutive independence day speeches between 1966 and 1976.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi , Union ministers and opposition leaders on Saturday extended Independence Day greetings to citizens as India marked its 80th Independence Day, with leaders remembering the freedom struggle while highlighting their visions for the country's future.Prime Minister Modi paid tribute to freedom fighters and said their courage and sacrifice continued to inspire India's journey towards a developed nation.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge , meanwhile, said constitutional values, democratic institutions and social harmony had faced "serious challenges" over the past decade.In a post on X, PM Modi paid tribute to the freedom fighters who fought against colonial rule and said their dreams continued to inspire the country."Warm greetings on the occasion of Independence Day. We remember with gratitude the countless freedom fighters whose courage, sacrifice and unwavering commitment ensured the end of colonial rule. Their dreams continue to inspire us as we work together to build a Viksit Bharat," he wrote.PM Modi added that India, "powered by 140 crore Indians", was scaling new heights of progress and expressed hope that the country's growth journey would accelerate further.Before his Independence Day address from the Red Fort, PM Modi also visited Raj Ghat and paid floral tributes to Mahatma Gandhi.Also read: PM Modi dons red tie-and-dye turban for Independence Day address The Prime Minister is leading the 80th Independence Day celebrations at the Red Fort, with this year's ceremony also marking 150 years of Vande Mataram and highlighting the role of youth in India's journey towards Viksit Bharat 2047.Union home minister Amit Shah also extended his greetings and paid tribute to those who sacrificed their lives during the freedom struggle."Heartfelt Independence Day greetings to all fellow citizens of the country," Shah said in a post on X.He said the country should use the occasion to resolve to accelerate the creation of a "developed, prosperous, and self-reliant India".Defence minister Rajnath Singh said the freedom struggle had given Indians not only political freedom but also the responsibility to shape the country's future.He called for a collective resolve to build a secure, strong, prosperous, self-reliant and developed India, while preserving its heritage and pursuing modernity, progress and innovation.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge struck a different note in his Independence Day message, saying India had made significant progress but that many aspirations remained unfulfilled."Over the past decade, our Constitutional values, democratic institutions and social harmony have faced serious challenges," Kharge said.He said freedom meant more than liberation from British rule and included the constitutional guarantees of equality, dignity, justice and freedom of expressionAlso read: 'Vande Mataram' played for first time as PM Modi addresses nation Kharge also called for greater opportunities for young people, dignity and justice for farmers, equality for women and the "full measure of equality and justice" for Dalits, Adivasis, OBCs, minorities and economically weaker sections.He said the country's greatest resolve on Independence Day should be "hope".Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav called on citizens to protect the Constitution, saying: "Freedom comes from the Constitution itself."He urged people to pledge to protect and uphold the continuity of the Constitution.NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar said the freedom secured through the sacrifices and patriotism of countless people was a responsibility for every citizen.He called for building a prosperous, capable and inclusive India while preserving constitutional values.Former Bihar chief minister Nitish Kumar also extended his "heartiest congratulations and best wishes" to people across the state and the country on Independence Day.The messages came as India marked 79 years since gaining independence from British rule in 1947, with political leaders across the spectrum remembering the freedom struggle while setting out differing visions for the country's future.

NEW DELHI: To mark India’s 80th Independence Day, Prime Minister Narendra Modi arrived at the Red Fort on Saturday wearing a striking red tie-and-dye turban with a long trailing end, as he delivered his 13th consecutive Independence Day address from the historic ramparts.The turban featured intricate red, green and white patterns, reflecting styles associated with Rajasthani and Gujarati traditions. He paired it with a white kurta-pajama and a brown jacket, completing the look with three pocket squares in saffron, white and green—the colours of the national flag.For more than a decade, PM Modi’s Independence Day appearances at the Red Fort have featured a closely watched visual tradition: the turban. Since his first address as Prime Minister in 2014, he has chosen safas and turbans in a wide range of colours, patterns and regional styles, often bringing India’s rich textile heritage and craftsmanship into focus.From Rajasthan’s bandhej and leheriya to tricolour-inspired designs, his choice of headgear has evolved from year to year while retaining its traditional character. Here is a look back at the distinctive turbans that have become a recognisable feature of Modi’s Independence Day appearances.For the 79th Independence Day, Modi opted for an all-saffron safa, paired with a white kurta and churidar, a saffron bandhgala jacket and a tricolour stole.The saffron turban marked his 12th consecutive Independence Day address from the historic Red Fort.In 2024, Modi chose a leheriya-print turban featuring bold orange, dark green and yellow streaks, with a long, deeply pleated tail.Leheriya is a traditional Rajasthani tie-dye textile known for its wave-like patterns, inspired by the movement of desert winds.Also read: 80th Independence Day: 'Vande Mataram' played for first time as PM Modi addresses nation Modi wore a multicoloured Rajasthani-style bandhani turban in 2023, featuring shades of yellow, green and red. The Prime Minister paired it with an off-white kurta-churidar, a black V-neck jacket and a geometric-patterned pocket square.In 2022, Modi aligned his Independence Day attire with the Har Ghar Tiranga campaign, wearing a white turban decorated with saffron and green stripes. He paired it with a white kurta-churidar and a baby-blue Nehru jacket.The headgear mirrored the colours of the national flag while retaining the traditional format associated with his Independence Day appearances.During the Covid-19 pandemic in 2021, Modi wore a saffron turban featuring bold red patterns and a long pink trail. He paired it with a white kurta, fitted churidar, deep blue jacket and a white scarf edged with a saffron border.The long trailing end remained a prominent feature of the headgear, continuing the distinctive visual style of his earlier Independence Day turbans.At the height of the Covid-19 pandemic, Modi chose a saffron-and-cream turban with an extended tail. He wore it with a white kurta and churidar, along with an orange-and-white stole that also served as a protective face covering.The ensemble combined his recurring use of traditional headgear with a practical response to the public-health circumstances of the time.In 2019, Modi wore a multicoloured safa featuring Rajasthan’s traditional leheriya wave pattern. The design created a ripple effect across the headgear and continued his use of regional textile traditions for the Independence Day occasion.In 2018, Modi returned to saffron, wearing a bright turban decorated with red patterns and a long trail that extended almost to his ankles.He paired the headgear with a white stole featuring a broad geometric-patterned border.Modi chose a vibrant yellow turban in 2017, featuring intricate traditional and geometric patterns woven across the fabric.The headgear combined bright red and yellow with a subtle golden criss-cross design.In 2016, Modi embraced the classic tie-and-dye technique with a vibrant bandhej turban in bright pink and yellow. The headgear featured distinctive patterns and a long trailing end.The festive design reflected the Prime Minister’s preference for colourful traditional headgear during the Independence Day celebrations.In 2015, Modi wore a sunny yellow turban covered in a multicoloured criss-cross pattern combining red and deep green. The headgear featured a long trail extending towards his ankles, giving the traditional Rajasthani-style turban a prominent silhouette.It marked another early example of Modi using Independence Day attire to foreground Indian textile traditions.For his maiden Independence Day address as Prime Minister in 2014, Modi wore a bright red Jodhpuri bandhej turban with contrasting green accents.The Rajasthani-style headgear featured vivid orange, yellow and green tones and traditional patterns. That first Red Fort appearance established the colourful turban as a recurring element of Modi’s Independence Day wardrobe, a tradition that has continued through successive addresses.
Article Summary: Pm modi wore a striking red tie-and-dye turban featuring yellow, green and white patterns for independence day. Since his first address as prime minister in 2014, he has chosen safas and turbans in a wide range of colours, patterns and regional styles. Modi wore a bright red jodhpuri bandhej turban for his maiden independence day address as prime minister in 2014.

Article Title: 'Greatest threat': How India, Pakistan view each other; data lays bare deep animosity
Article Text:
A survey has revealed that a majority of adults in Pakistan and India view the other as their single greatest threat.

' Greatest threat ': India and Pakistan point at each other

The data paints a stark picture of two neighbours frozen in mutual distrust.

Mutual hostility runs deep

The numbers on bilateral perceptions are stark.

Lack of trust

When asked whether the Indian and Pakistani governments and people are committed to good relations with each other, the clear pattern is that people only have faith in their own country Pew Research report

Beneath the geopolitical differences lies a more fundamental problem: the absence of trust.

How Bangladesh, Sri Lanka view the rivals

The India-Pakistan divide extends beyond bilateral relations.

Divergent worldviews

Two countries, two very different worlds

Nearly eight decades after the 1947 Partition of British India gave birth to two independent nations, deep-seated historical trauma, and territorial disputes that have led to multiple military confrontations continue to shape the mindset of citizens on both sides of the border.As the two countries celebrate their independence, a major survey by the Pew Research Center reveals that an overwhelming majority of adults in both nuclear-armed rivals view the other as their single greatest geopolitical threat.Conducted across South Asia between February and May 2026, the findings highlight a persistent, deep-rooted mutual hostility that shows little sign of thawing. These sentiments reflect not merely political disagreements, but deeply entrenched unfavourable opinions among general populations, extending into perceptions of global superpowers, regional allies, and the long-term prospects for bilateral peace.The data paints a stark picture of two neighbours frozen in mutual distrust.In India, 54% of respondents named Pakistan as the greatest threat to their country.Conversely, 43% of Pakistanis identified India as their primary security threat.For Indians, China is the next most cited threat at 21%. For Pakistanis, Israel and the US each register at 24% as major threats — though still far below India.These threat perceptions align closely with how each public judges the other’s commitment to peace.Most Indians believe their own government and people are committed to good bilateral relations, but a majority say Pakistan’s government and people are not.Pakistanis mirror this: they express confidence in their own side’s commitment but doubt India’s.The numbers on bilateral perceptions are stark.Nearly nine in 10 Pakistanis have an unfavourable view of India, with 73% describing their opinion as 'very unfavourable'. The sentiment cuts across demographic groups, suggesting that hostility toward India is not confined to any particular section of Pakistani society.The picture in India is similarly bleak. As many as 78% of Indians have an unfavourable view of Pakistan, including 65% who hold a very unfavourable opinion. There is, however, a notable internal divide in India. Indian Muslims are somewhat more favorable toward Pakistan (21%) than Indian Hindus (6%), and they are also less likely to name Pakistan as their top threat (34% vs 57% among Hindus).Pew's polling also shows that this is not a temporary shift in sentiment.Indian views of Pakistan have remained overwhelmingly negative for more than a decade, with the share expressing a favourable opinion never rising above 20% since 2013.Historical Pew surveys also show that Pakistanis have long held predominantly negative views of India. Pakistani respondents expressing favourable views of India have generally ranged from single digits to around one-third.The survey further suggests that hostility is not simply about how Indians and Pakistanis perceive each other. It also extends to whether they believe the other side genuinely wants better relations.A clear pattern emerges: people tend to believe that their own government and population are committed to good bilateral relations, while doubting the intentions of the other side.A majority of Indians believe both the Indian government and Indian people are committed to maintaining good relations with Pakistan. But a majority of Pakistanis reject that assessment, saying the Indian government and people are not committed to good relations.The mirror image appears in Pakistan.A majority of Pakistanis say their government and people want good relations with India.Most Indians, however, believe Pakistan's government and people are not committed to improving ties. About a quarter of Indian respondents were unsure.This mutual lack of trust creates a difficult cycle: each side sees itself as willing to improve relations while viewing the other as unwilling to reciprocate.Indian Muslims again stand apart to some degree. Around a third say the Pakistani government and people are committed to good relations, significantly higher than the corresponding share among Indian Hindus.The Pew findings become even more revealing when India and Pakistan are placed alongside Bangladesh and Sri Lanka.Of the four South Asian countries surveyed, Sri Lanka is the only country that receives more positive than negative ratings from respondents in all three of the others.India, meanwhile, has the widest range of perceptions.Sri Lankans are overwhelmingly positive toward India, with 79% expressing a favourable opinion. In Bangladesh, 42% view India favourably. In Pakistan, however, the figure plunges to just 7%.India is also seen as Sri Lanka's most important ally by a clear majority: 63% of Sri Lankan respondents name India.The picture is very different in Bangladesh and Pakistan, where India is most often identified as the greatest threat.Views of Prime Minister Narendra Modi follow a broadly similar pattern. Seventy percent of Sri Lankans express confidence in PM Modi to do the right thing in world affairs, compared with 42% in Bangladesh and 4% in Pakistan.The survey also finds that Pakistan is not universally viewed negatively across South Asia.Fifty-seven percent of Sri Lankans and 54% of Bangladeshis have a favourable opinion of Pakistan, compared with only 8% of Indians.Bangladesh itself receives broadly positive views in Pakistan and Sri Lanka: 66% of Pakistanis and 56% of Sri Lankans express favourable opinions of Bangladesh. Only about a quarter of Indians do so.Sri Lanka emerges as the region's relative outlier. Around half or more of respondents in India, Pakistan and Bangladesh view the island nation positively, while significantly fewer hold negative views.The India-Pakistan divide extends beyond bilateral relations to the way each country views the global order.For Indians, Russia remains a particularly important and popular partner. Thirty-six percent identify Russia as India's most important ally, while 16% name the United States.Russia's favourable image in India is particularly striking. Fifty-eight percent of Indians have a favourable opinion of Russia, while 51% express confidence in Russian President Vladimir Putin.Pakistanis are considerably less positive: 39% have a favourable view of Russia and only 32% express confidence in Putin.India's relationship with the United States is also reflected in public opinion. Indians are substantially more favourable toward the US than Pakistanis are and are more likely to express confidence in US President Donald Trump.The picture is almost completely reversed when it comes to China.An overwhelming 90% of Pakistanis have a favourable view of China, while 83% express confidence in Chinese President Xi Jinping. Three-quarters of Pakistanis identify China as their country's most important ally.Saudi Arabia is a distant second, named by 12%.In India, however, only around a quarter of respondents view China or Xi positively. Even Indian Muslims, who are more favourable toward China than Indian Hindus, remain negative toward both China and its president on balance.Nearly 80 years after Partition, the survey suggests that the India-Pakistan rivalry remains deeply embedded not only in government policy and military strategy, but also in public perceptions.The most striking finding may therefore not be that Indians and Pakistanis dislike each other. It is that both overwhelmingly believe the other side sees them as the problem.That mutual conviction — reinforced by decades of conflict, competing national narratives and geopolitical rivalry — remains one of the biggest barriers to changing the relationship between the two nuclear-armed neighbours.Yet beneath these geopolitical differences lies a more fundamental problem: the absence of trust.Both populations believe their own side is committed to better relations, while doubting the intentions of the other.
Article Summary: A majority of adults in pakistan and india view the other as their single greatest threat. The data paints a stark picture of two neighbours frozen in mutual distrust. People tend to believe that their own government and population are committed to good bilateral relations, while doubting the intentions of the other side.

Article Title: 'Not said, but presented as if it was': CJI Surya Kant says 'cockroach' remark 'misquoted'
Article Text:
CJI Surya Kant said his 'cockroach' remark was 'misquoted and misused' through clipped court videos, warning against misleading social media posts.

NEW DELHI: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant has said that his oral remarks during a Supreme Court hearing were “misquoted” and later used with “malicious intent” to mislead the country’s youth, amid controversy over a comment that sparked the satirical online movement “Cockroach Janta Party”."My comment was misquoted and misused. What was not said is presented as though it was said. This is extremely unfortunate. Particularly, it is a major malicious attempt to mislead the youth of the country," Kant in a DD News interview.Kant expressed concern over short clips of court proceedings being circulated on social media without the necessary context."You are on social media, print media or any form of media or you are simply a citizen. All of us have rights and constitutional duty and responsibilities," he further said."When we speak of rights, we must also possess the capacity to fulfil our obligations. Therefore, I would urge them to keep their responsibilities in mind; we must all make tireless efforts to ensure that harmony prevails in society," he added.On May 15, while hearing a case in the Supreme Court, Kant had compared certain individuals with fraudulent degrees to “cockroaches” who become social media or RTI activists to attack the system.The remarks triggered widespread backlash among young people and inspired the satirical “Cockroach Janta Party” (CJP) movement.The CJP later led protests at Jantar Mantar over the NEET-UG paper leak. The over-a-month-long agitation culminated in a clash between protesters and police on July 20, leaving several people injured on both sides. The protests also preceded the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.
Article Summary: Cji surya kant said his 'cockroach' remark was'misquoted and misused' through clipped court videos, warning against misleading social media posts. On may 15, while hearing a case in the supreme court, kant had compared certain individuals with fraudulent degrees to “cockroaches” who become social media or rti activists to attack the system.

Article Title: We have strong ties with Italy, should be respectful: MEA on Congress leader's 'Meloni' remark
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs on Friday called to 'respect India's ties with Italy' over remarks made by Congress leader Sandeep Dikshit, while mocking PM Modi's foreign policy."We have strong ties with Italy. Our ties with Italy in recent years have expanded and strengthened in every which way, and it’s important that, as part of diplomatic practice, we strengthen our ties, keeping in mind and being respectful of each other. There’s mutual understanding between the two sides," said MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal.The remarks came a day after Rahul Gandhi criticised Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s approach to foreign policy at the Rachnatmak Congress national convention in New Delhi. Gandhi said he did not understand the idea that “foreign policy means hugging leaders” and used a hug with Congress leader Sandeep Dikshit to illustrate his point. Dikshit then brought Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni into the exchange, asking, “You weren’t hugging me thinking I was Meloni?” to which Rahul replied, “I haven’t reached that stage yet,” drawing laughter from the gathering.Rahul then returned to his broader criticism of the Modi government’s foreign policy, questioning India’s role in the West Asia conflict and saying Pakistan had stepped in as a mediator between the US and Iran while India “simply looked on.” He also criticised the government’s handling of the India-China border situation, alleging that China had prevented Indian forces from patrolling certain areas in Arunachal Pradesh.

91% indegenisation in Army ammunitions

NEW DELHI: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Friday said India's defence sector had undergone an “unprecedented transformation” over the past 12 years, with domestic defence production rising nearly fourfold to a record Rs 1.78 lakh crore in 2025-26.In his message to soldiers on the eve of Independence Day, Rajnath said India had reduced its dependence on defence imports while strengthening indigenous manufacturing under the Aatmanirbhar Bharat and Make in India initiatives.""You all know that under the leadership of the Hon'ble Prime Minister, our government has always accorded the highest priority to self-reliance in the defence sector. Over the past 12 years, you have witnessed unprecedented transformation in the defence sector through Aatmanirbhar Bharat and Make in India," he said.“Our domestic defence production, which stood at around Rs 46,000 crore in 2014, reached a record Rs 1.78 lakh crore in FY 2025-26. This means that over the past decade, our domestic defence production has increased nearly fourfold. This is proof of the structural changes that have taken place over the past decade," the defence minister added.The union minister further highlighted recent tests and developments in indigenous defence technology, including the MIRV-equipped Advanced Agni missile, Rudram-II air-to-surface missile, Long Range Land Attack Cruise Missile and Pinaka Long Range Guided Rocket.“We have also made major advances in hypersonic technology. The successful demonstration of Solid Fuel Ducted Ramjet technology is equally significant,” he said.He also said the first successful test of the indigenous Kusha Long Range Surface-to-Air Missile had strengthened India's air-defence capabilities.As Rajnath hailed the growth in defence sector, the ministry of defence said India's defence production reached a record Rs 1.78 lakh crore in 2025-26, nearly four times the level of 2014. The government said defence exports have grown 56-fold, from Rs 686 crore in 2013-14 to Rs 38,424 crore in 2025-26, with Indian defence products now reaching more than 80 countries.The defence budget has increased 3.1-fold, from Rs 2.53 lakh crore in 2013-14 to Rs 7.85 lakh crore in 2026-27, while capital expenditure has risen 2.3-fold to Rs 2.19 lakh crore. Defence R&D spending has more than doubled to Rs 29,100 crore in 2026-27 from Rs 13,716 crore in 2014-15.The ministry said the Indian Army has achieved roughly 91% self-sufficiency in ammunition, having indigenised 159 of 175 ammunition variants.The government is targeting Rs 3 lakh crore in annual defence production and Rs 50,000 crore in defence exports by 2029.

Domestic defence production has risen nearly fourfold to a record rs 1.78 lakh crore in 2025-26. Defence exports have grown 56-fold, with indian defence products reaching more than 80 countries.

Article Title: 'Cannot imagine': Rajnath Singh's sharp 'Gandhi surname' attack on Rahul Gandhi over PM hug jibe
Article Text:
Rajnath Singh said he was particularly upset that the comments came from the Lok Sabha LoP.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Defence minister Rajnath Singh has hit back at Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over his remarks on Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the government's foreign policy, calling them “petty and condemnable” and warning that such language could damage democratic discourse.Singh said he was particularly upset that the comments came from the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha. He accused Gandhi of lowering the dignity associated with the post and questioned whether such conduct was appropriate for someone holding a key constitutional position."The remarks made by LoP Rahul Gandhi on PM Narendra Modi and India's foreign policy yesterday are petty and condemnable. It is painful for me personally, too. In my long political life, I had never seen such indecent and unimaginable conduct from any LoP. Such conduct is a grave sign of a threat to a healthy democracy," Singh said.The defence minister also defended Modi's record as Prime Minister and his standing abroad, while arguing that political differences should not lead to what he described as disrespectful remarks."Rahul Gandhi might have frustration with PM in his mind, but such indecent remarks are unacceptable, especially when PM Modi has been a Prime Minister who has brought prestige to India nationally and internationally, and paved the way for Viksit Bharat. ""In 12 years, working with full dedication, he did not take any leave.Such indecent remarks against such a PM pain every Indian," he said.Singh then turned his criticism towards the Congress, questioning whether the party could continue to claim the legacy of several of India's prominent leaders after Gandhi's remarks."I would also like to humbly tell the Congress party that after such language and conduct, can they have any claim over the legacy of Lal-Bal-Pal and Gandhi, Patel and Nehru, from Subhas Babu to Rajendra Babu and Shastri ji and Narasimha Rao ji to Pranab Mukherjee?" Rajnath Singh said.He further accused Gandhi of not only targeting Modi but also damaging India's image and the dignity of the Leader of Opposition's office."With this conduct, Rahul Gandhi has not only insulted PM Narendra Modi but also the international prestige of India. He has shredded the dignity of the post of Lok Sabha LoP. I cannot even imagine that someone with the Gandhi surname can make such a shameful remark."The exchange followed remarks made by Gandhi at the Congress's Rachnatmak Congress National Convention in New Delhi on Thursday.Gandhi criticised the government's approach to foreign policy and argued that India's international relations should be driven by national interest rather than personal relationships between political leaders."I don't know where it came from; this idea got into their heads. I don't know who put it there or where it came from, the idea that foreign policy means hugging politicians. I was young. We went to America. Since we're talking about expressions, I'll share this. We went to America. I was twelve years old. Priyanka, myself, my mother, and my grandmother - my grandmother was the Prime Minister. There was a state dinner - an official dinner. My grandmother and mother went to the official dinner," he said.He added, "You aren't just visiting a friend's house. In this role, the Prime Minister of India doesn't engage in mere friendship. They have no interest in friendship; their job is to protect the country."Gandhi also accused the Modi government of damaging India's foreign policy, using the ongoing conflict involving Iran, the US and Israel as an example."War broke out in Iran. For India - had it recognised its own strength and had its leader been someone like Indira Gandhi--this presented the greatest opportunity in the world. What kind of opportunity? Iran was our old friend, America was our friend, and Russia was our friend. We could have stepped up, become relevant, and leveraged these friendships. But what actually happened? Nothing of the sort. Instead, Pakistan stepped in and took our place; Pakistan became the mediator, while India and Modi-ji simply looked on," he said.Rahul Gandhi claimed he receives "information directly from Modi ji's office these days; there is a full-blown revolt going on inside".He also referred to certain claims in videos on social media about China's actions concerning patrolling along the LAC in a border area of Arunachal Pradesh.He also raised allegations concerning Chinese activity along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in Arunachal Pradesh and accused the government of pressuring the media not to report certain claims."In our patrolling areas--specifically in Arunachal--China blocked us from patrolling. They essentially said, 'Look, all that is fine--it is indeed your land--but you cannot patrol here.' Rajnath Singh, Amit Shah, and Narendra Modi have been completely deflated. They are calling up all the media editors, telling them, 'Don't publish this in your newspapers; suppress the story.' They are causing direct harm to the country without a second thought," he said.Gandhi also revisited the dispute over India's handling of the border situation with China following the Galwan clash.He alleged that conflicting statements about whether Indian territory had been lost weakened India's position during negotiations with China."After the Galwan incident, the Prime Minister held a meeting--a Zoom call. He stated that China hadn't taken a single inch of Indian territory. The Army said that our land had been taken. Just think about the message sent to China: Chinese negotiators asked our negotiators, 'What nonsense are you talking about? Your own Prime Minister said no land was lost.' So, internally, they have destroyed the country; they have wrecked our foreign policy. And they did all of this solely to finance their political structure, to secure funds from Adaniji," he alleged.
Article Summary: Rajnath singh said he was particularly upset that the comments came from the lok sabha lop. He accused gandhi of lowering the dignity associated with the post and questioned whether such conduct was appropriate for someone holding a key constitutional position.

Article Title: SC quashes all FIRs against Samay Raina, Ranveer Allahabadia in ‘India’s Got Latent’ case
Article Text:
SC quashes all FIRs against Samay Raina, Ranveer Allahbadia

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday closed criminal proceedings against comedian Samay Raina and four other social media personalities over remarks concerning people with disabilities, while recognising their subsequent efforts to promote awareness and dignity for the community.Along with Raina, the court quashed the FIRs and related proceedings against comedians Vipul Goyal, Balraj Paramjeet Singh Ghai, Sonali Thakkar and Nishant Jagdish Tanwar.The proceedings stemmed from jokes made by the five, which were flagged by the M/s SMA Cure Foundation, an organisation working with people affected by Spinal Muscular Atrophy and other rare diseases.The case took a different turn after the Supreme Court asked the influencers to take constructive steps towards supporting people with disabilities. The court noted that they had since organised a chess tournament for specially-abled people in March and helped raise awareness about organisations working with people with disabilities.The bench, comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, said their efforts appeared to be producing positive results."Once there are genuine efforts, positive results are bound to be there," the bench said as per news agency PTI."They are very bright youngsters. If they have started working in the positive direction, they will bring positive results," it added.Senior advocate Aparajita Singh, appearing for the SMA Cure Foundation, told the court that the influencers had made "genuine efforts" and had attempted to engage with the foundation following the court's earlier intervention."This matter was going nowhere till this court took a very strong stand last time," Singh said.The court subsequently quashed the FIRs and other criminal proceedings against the five and said their case was now closed.However, the Supreme Court said it would separately examine the larger question of how the dignity of people with disabilities can be better protected and whether comprehensive directions are required.The court's observations came a day after the CJI and other judges met a delegation of people with disabilities from different fields."It was quite a learning and an eye-opener for us also," the CJI said, adding, "We have requested them to send their suggestions also.""It was quite a satisfying experience what we saw yesterday and what we interacted," he said.The delegation included 20 people, among them Paralympians and athletes such as Nidhi Mishra, Ankur Dhama and Major D P Singh, as well as Chhonzin Angmo.During Friday's hearing, the bench also noted that the influencers had engaged in meaningful discussions with the SMA Cure Foundation and were willing to invite people living with SMA to their shows.More programmes are also planned to raise funds for people affected by the condition.The influencers had earlier volunteered before the Supreme Court in November to organise at least two events every month, either online or in person, to raise money for a proposed corpus that could provide financial assistance to people living with SMA.The court's decision therefore brings the criminal proceedings against the five to an end, while leaving the broader question of protecting the dignity of people with disabilities open for further consideration.
Article Summary: Sc quashes all firs against samay raina, ranveer allahbadia, vipul goyal, balraj paramjeet singh ghai, sonali thakkar and nishant jagdish tanwar. The court noted that they had since organised a chess tournament for specially-abled people in march and helped raise awareness about organisations working with people with disabilities.

Article Title: Iran president Pezeshkian to visit India for BRICS summit amid Middle East tensions
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian, amid the elevated tensions in West Asia, is set to visit New Delhi to attend the upcoming BRICS summit, Iranian sources told news agency ANI.Pezeshkian's participation in the summit is scheduled to be held in the national capital in September.The visit assumes significance as India is hosting the 18th BRICS Summit under its 2026 chairship. The summit will be held under India's theme of "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability". India assumed the BRICS chairship from Brazil at the beginning of 2026.Iran has signalled that it sees India as a potential partner in efforts to ease tensions in West Asia, with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi saying New Delhi could play a greater role in de-escalating the ongoing crisis.Araghchi made the remarks during his visit to India in June for the BRICS foreign ministers' Meeting. Speaking to reporters in New Delhi, he said Tehran did not see a military solution to the conflict and believed that negotiations offered the only viable way forward.“We will welcome any constructive role by India,” Araghchi said, signalling Iran's openness to an Indian role in diplomatic efforts.His comments came as fighting and tensions continue to shape the security situation in West Asia following the outbreak of conflict on February 28 between Iran and the combined forces of the United States and Israel.India's relationship with Iran has also been marked by regular high-level engagement. In October 2024, Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian met Prime Minister Narendra Modi on the sidelines of the BRICS summit in Kazan, Russia. The two leaders discussed bilateral ties as well as developments in the region.Iran became a full member of BRICS in 2024, joining Egypt, Ethiopia and the United Arab Emirates as part of the group's expansion. Indonesia became a full member in 2025, taking the total number of members to 11.During his latest visit, Araghchi also met external affairs minister S Jaishankar to discuss regional developments and Iran's position on security around the Strait of Hormuz.Araghchi said Iran would continue to fulfil what he described as its historical responsibility for security in the strategically important waterway. He also sought to reassure countries that maintain friendly relations with Tehran about the safety of their commercial activity.“In fruitful engagement with my host external affairs minister S Jaishankar, discussed regional developments and clarified that Iran will always carry out historical duty as protector of security in Hormuz. Iran is a reliable partner of all friendly nations, who can rely on safety of commerce.”The Iranian government also highlighted Araghchi's intervention at the BRICS meeting, where he spoke about reducing Western dominance and preventing political considerations from influencing international institutions.“FM Seyyed Abbas Araghchi delivers Iran's statement at the BRICS foreign ministers' meeting in India. He highlighted the importance of breaking Western hegemony and ensuring that international institutions remain free from political manipulation.”The statements come at a time when West Asia remains caught in a fragile stalemate, with tensions continuing to simmer amid the wider conflict between Iran and the United States and Israel. For India, Tehran's invitation for a constructive role adds another dimension to its diplomatic engagement with both Iran and the wider region.
Article Summary: Pezeshkian's participation in the summit is scheduled to be held in the national capital in september. The visit assumes significance as india is hosting the 18th brics summit under its 2026 chairship. Iran has signalled that it sees india as a potential partner in efforts to ease tensions in west asia.

Article Title: ‘Congress responsible for Partition’: CM Yogi says India would be different if Modi were PM in 1947
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath has accused the Congress of being responsible for India's Partition and the violence that followed, arguing that the country's history could have been different under leaders such as Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel or Prime Minister Narendra Modi.Speaking at an event in Lucknow marking Partition Horrors Remembrance Day, CM Yogi said the Congress had failed the country by prioritising political power and alleged that the consequences of Partition continue to affect India.“Had Narendra Modi been the Prime Minister of India at the time of Independence, nobody would have been able to damage India in the slightest,” he was quoted as saying by news agency PTI.He also invoked Patel, saying that a leader of his stature would not have allowed India to be divided.“If a person like Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel were the Prime Minister at that time, nobody would have been able to disintegrate India ... The country had to pay a heavy price for the cowardice of these Congress members -- a character you all witnessed during the CAA protests,” he added.Adityanath alleged that areas including Sindh, Punjab and Bengal were handed over to Pakistan despite what he described as their Hindu and regional demographic character.“Bengal was Bengali-dominated. All Hindu villages were forcibly given to Bangladesh. This shameful act was committed by the Congress, which was extra-restless for power, and on whom the country had reposed its trust. It repaid that trust with betrayal,” he said.The chief minister also criticised the Congress over its response to attacks on Hindus in Bangladesh. He alleged that the party remained silent because it was concerned about losing electoral support.“They feared that reacting to the events in Bangladesh might cause their vote bank here to drift away. To them, the murder of Dalit Hindus holds no significance; what matters is their own vote bank,” he said.Adityanath further argued that internal divisions based on caste, region and language had historically weakened India and created opportunities for outside forces.“When such infighting exists, then conspiracy easily creeps in,” he said.He said the consequences of Partition could still be seen in the form of terrorism, Naxalism, Maoism and extremism. He also questioned the Congress's claims about its role in India's freedom struggle and accused the party of presenting itself as indispensable to the creation of modern India.“This also draws our attention to the silence we have all maintained regarding that pre-1947 conspiracy. Yet, even today, these people move before society, acting as if they were the ones who created India, and that without them, India would not have come into existence. It is a truly strange situation,” he said, describing Partition as the “darkest chapter of humanity.”Turning to what he described as the Congress's political legacy, Adityanath said institutions across the country had been named after one political family.“Every institution in the country came to bear the name of that very clan. Every single institution was named after that clan, and we all stood by silently, merely watching. What are they doing even today? What are their actions like now?” he said.The UP chief minister also defended the Citizenship Amendment Act and attacked the Congress's opposition to it.“There was no justification for opposing the act. The act contained a provision regarding Afghanistan, Pakistan, and Bangladesh -- territories that were once part of undivided India and share a heritage spanning thousands of years. It stipulated that if a Hindu, Sikh, Jain, Buddhist, Parsi, or Christian from these countries had been forced to leave and had sought refuge in India for five years, they would be granted Indian citizenship,” he said.He argued that the legislation did not provide for taking away land or property from Muslims or political parties, and accused opponents of using the issue to provoke protests.“Nowhere did it say that we would seize land belonging to Muslims, the Congress, or the Samajwadi Party. There was no such provision in the Act. Yet, attempts were made to incite agitation across the country,” he said.Adityanath also targeted the Samajwadi Party, claiming that Uttar Pradesh would have witnessed widespread unrest had it been in power during the CAA protests.“What kind of unbridled mayhem would have taken place? The rioters knew the price they would have to pay, which is why they could not act as they pleased; yet, their audacity was evident,” he said.“If you wish to see their true character, you would have witnessed it during the CAA protests, and their silence regarding the recent events in Bangladesh once again puts them in the dock,” Adityanath said.The event also featured a silent march led by Adityanath and other party leaders from the statue of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel to Lok Bhavan, according to the Uttar Pradesh government.
Article Summary: Cm yogi adityanath said the congress had failed the country by prioritising political power. He alleged that areas including sindh, punjab and bengal were handed over to pakistan. He also criticised the congress over its response to attacks on hindus in bangladesh.

From then till today we are suffering the consequences of this Indus Waters Treaty,” Omar said, adding that under the treaty J&K could neither extract drinking water from the Chenab nor use the Jhelum for irrigation or building a barrage at Tulbul. “Our blood has been sucked and now the IWT has been cancelled.This should remain cancelled so that we can use this water properly,” Omar added.The IWT was signed between India and Pakistan in 1960. Under the treaty, India received full rights to use the waters of the three eastern rivers, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej, while Pakistan received rights over the three western rivers, Indus, Chenab and Jhelum.India placed the treaty in abeyance last year following the Pahalgam terror attack. In May last year, after the treaty was placed in abeyance, Omar called for restarting the Tulbul Navigation Project on Wular Lake in north Kashmir. The project is located on Wular Lake in the Sopore area of Baramulla district. Pakistan has opposed construction of a 439-foot-long, 40-foot-wide barrage, also known as the Wular barrage or Tulbul Navigation Project, with a navigation lock on the lake.The Union govt began work on the project in 1984 to regulate water levels and facilitate navigation. However, work was halted a year later after Pakistan objected. Pakistan raised the issue with the Indus Waters Commission in 1986 and work was stopped in 1987.The governing National Conference in J&K has opposed the IWT all along, calling it detrimental to the interests of the people of Jammu and Kashmir.
